24 Ashad 2083
Thursday
Meeting (Second)

The second meeting of the National Assembly today commenced at 16:41 hours under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Members,
(16:41 hrs)
I have made a minor change to today's agenda for the second meeting of the National Assembly. Honourable Members, I now provide the floor to the Honourable Minister of Finance, Dr. Swarnim Wagle, to present the proposal for discussion on the Property Dilution (Money Laundering) Prevention (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083, which has been received with a message from the House of Representatives along with the report of the Legislation Management Committee.
Honourable Minister of Finance Dr. Swarnim Wagle:- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(16:42 hrs)
With the permission of the Chairperson, I present before this Honourable House the proposal for discussion on the Property Dilution (Money Laundering) Prevention (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083, received with a message from the House of Representatives along with the report of the Legislation Management Committee. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Members, I now present the said proposal for decision. Honourable Members in favour of this proposal will say "Aye" and Honourable Members against it will say "Nay".
Honourable Members in favour of this proposal, say "Aye".
- "Aye"
Honourable Members against this proposal, say "Nay".
No "Nay" voices were heard. Therefore, I declare that the proposal for discussion on the Property Dilution (Money Laundering) Prevention (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083, along with the report of the Legislation Management Committee, received with a message from the House of Representatives, has been unanimously approved.
Honourable Members, discussion will now take place on the Property Dilution (Money Laundering) Prevention (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083, along with the report of the Legislation Management Committee, received with a message from the House of Representatives. I inform you that discussion can only be held on the committee's report and the related clauses of the bill, as well as other consequential clauses.
I request Honourable Members who wish to speak to submit their names within two minutes. I have allocated three minutes to each Honourable Member participating in the discussion. Honourable Member Khamma Bahadur Khati.
Honourable Mr. Khamma Bahadur Khati (Nepali Congress):- Right Honourable Chairperson, Honourable Ministers, and Honourable Members, I wish to raise a few points regarding the Property Dilution (Money Laundering) Prevention (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083. Firstly, regarding the third amendment to the Property Dilution (Money Laundering) Prevention Act, extensive discussions were held in the Legislation Committee. With the direct involvement, consultation, and suggestions of the Honourable Minister of Finance, the proposals we put forth had only two clauses. The Minister also facilitated the process in a very easy, simple, and smooth manner. Feedback was received from all Honourable Members. This alone is not sufficient; there are many shortcomings. These will be addressed later in a manner that adapts to the time, circumstances, and events. However, considering the discussions we have had and the amendments we proposed for swift justice, it was agreed that Clause 13, Sub-clause 1, Clause (c) should remain as per the previous provision, and similarly, regarding Clause 22, Sub-clause 1, the publication by the government through a notice in the Nepal Gazette would be an encroachment of jurisdiction, so it was agreed to publish it with the words "Attorney General's Office".
Thus, through discussions among the Ministers and Honourable Members, we have reached a conclusion. This has taken concrete form. In the coming days, our problem was that due to insufficient time, many Honourable Members could not express their views. The time was short. In the coming days, may this come on time and the discussion process proceed in this manner, and may the Upper House, by keeping the public at the center of policy and rule-making, not only facilitate but also contribute to amending the existing laws and regulations received from the House of Representatives, which is commendable. For this, I thank the Minister of Finance and other ministers who showed goodwill and expressed their views, and we have realized that even though it came as a replacement bill from an ordinance, it has come with amendments, and they have also realized this. I have said this much, thank you, Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Members, the discussion on the proposal for discussion on the Property Dilution (Money Laundering) Prevention (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083, along with the report of the Legislation Management Committee, received with a message from the House of Representatives, concludes here.
Honourable Members, I now provide the floor to the Honourable Minister of Finance, Dr. Swarnim Wagle, to respond to the questions raised during the discussion.
Honourable Minister of Finance Dr. Swarnim Wagle:- Right Honourable Chairperson,
(16:48 hrs)
I will not say much. Honourable Khamma Bahadur Khati has already said it. We have advanced this law-making process in a harmonious and judicious manner. We should continue this in the future as well. The National Assembly has a special place in our federal parliament. It is known as the "Upper House," and we expect constructive support from the Honourable Members here. I believe that even amidst time constraints and the pressure of simultaneously addressing national needs, we have found an excellent way forward, which will help the country progress. Therefore, I extend my heartfelt thanks to the Honourable Members, the Right Honourable Chairperson, and all the staff. Thank you.

Honorable Shri Renu Chand (Nepal Communist Party): (16:56 hrs) Honorable Chairperson, the act of getting bills passed in such haste impacts the quality of law. The bill was being amended when it reached the committee. We are forced to pass this in haste and bear the responsibility for its legal consequences, Mr. Speaker. The government has new colleagues; they at least have the convenience of being new, but we don't even have that. When the public questions us later, asking what we were doing, the moral responsibility will fall entirely on us. Therefore, I urge the respected Chairperson, the honorable Chairperson, and the government not to put us in such a situation in the future. For example, what happens when we are not allowed to read, not given enough time? For instance, it was written in Clause 33 (b) that there will be a Government Procurement Service Office under the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers' Office. Provisions like these show a lack of understanding of federalism and interfere with the jurisdiction of provincial and local governments, so extensive discussions were held and some improvements were made. The National Assembly is the house of federalism. When such issues arise, we must be accountable to our people and to our electorate. Although the facilitation by the ministers was beneficial to us, if you had passed it without allowing us to read, when we go to the electorate, they will ask us, 'You were old, experienced. What did you do?' and we will have no moral ground to stand on. Such matters need to be considered in the future, this is my request. The government also needs to understand that the Legislation Committee, the National Assembly, is an opportunity to correct its mistakes and the mistakes in the law. The National Assembly has its nature and history. It has always facilitated and refined the government's work. Therefore, even though this act has come in a hurry, and even though we haven't been able to discuss it extensively, with the cooperation of all of us, the government ministers, the committee chairperson, the committee members, and the amendment proposers, through extensive discussion – extensive because we are compelled to use the word 'extensive' due to sitting from morning till evening. However, even that morning-to-evening sitting was not enough. Keeping this in mind for the future, I would like to thank the ministers, the committee chairperson, the members, and all the amendment proposers. I urge you to pass this, thank you. Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dahal (Nepal Communist Party, UML): (17:08 hrs) Honorable Chairperson, we are now going to have further discussions in relation to the Bill to Amend the Cooperatives Act, 2074, the Cooperatives Bill, 2083, after it has come from the Legislation Management Committee. I myself and 9 other honorable members had submitted amendments to various clauses in this Legislation Management Committee. Honorable members who submitted amendments, honorable members of the committee, the leadership of the ministry, and the honorable minister himself, along with the concerned civil servants, we had intense discussions and interactions, and our common objective, the objective of the honorable members, the objective of the honorable members who submitted amendments, and the objective of the ministry leadership, was to make this bill better, to make it more advanced and refined. Therefore, our participation there was meaningful, all of us participated meaningfully, and the ministry truly took ownership. It took ownership, and most of the issues raised by us, most of the issues raised by the honorable members who submitted amendments, have been addressed. Our concern was singular. How to organize and manage the capital, skills, and technology of small cooperatives scattered in villages, how to manage the 30-32 thousand cooperatives operating in the country, how to establish good governance there, and how to strengthen this sector, which involves millions of people, in line with our constitution's vision of a three-pillar economy: public, private, and cooperative, and how to increase its role in the economy. We remained focused on this. Therefore, despite the time constraints, we had intense discussions and interactions, day and night, and it has been presented to the house after being passed unanimously. Therefore, I request and urge all honorable members to pass this bill unanimously. I also extend my thanks to the honorable minister and all the staff of the Parliament Secretariat. Thank you. Honorable Mr. Basudev Ghimire (Nepali Congress): - Honorable Chairperson, (17:21 hrs) We discussed the Bill to Amend Some Nepal Acts related to Health Sciences Institute, 2083 in the Legislation Management Committee yesterday, and in a short time, we have reached some decisions by having intensive discussions to make it better. The Honorable Minister of Health and Population has also taken ownership of the amendment proposals raised by us, the amendment proposers, on behalf of the government, so we also support it. Under Section 2, in the words "recommendation of the Vice-Chancellor" in Sub-section (1) of Section 11 (c) of the BP Koirala Health Sciences Institute Act, 2049, the Honorable Minister of Health and Population has accepted the amendment and replaced the words "as per the procedure formulated by the Ministry" which were passed by the House of Representatives and are in effect, with the words "as per the procedure formulated by the Executive Committee". 2. Honorable members, the House of Representatives passed the Public Procurement (Second Amendment) Bill, 2083, the Anti-Money Laundering (Second Amendment) Bill, 2083, and the Cooperatives Bill, which were sent to the committee on Ashad 23, 2083.

The First Amendment Bill, 2083 and the Bill to Amend Some Nepal Laws Related to the Health Sciences Establishment, 2083, have been presented to the House from the committee under strict time constraints and have been passed by the House today. In this short period leading up to the passing stage, the committee members, under the leadership of the Chairperson of the Legislative Management Committee, have actively played their roles. Similarly, I express my heartfelt thanks to the honorable members of the House, the concerned honorable ministers, the civil servants of the committee secretariat, and the employees of the concerned bodies for the significant roles they have played. I also expect that the committee will continue to be active in enhancing the dignity of the National Assembly in the future. Today, the National Assembly can proudly state that it has succeeded in discussing four replacement bills in the committee and sending them to the House of Representatives after discussing and passing two dependent bills (the Finance Bill, 2083 and the Debt Raising Bill, 2083) in the House in a single day. Finally, I would like to thank everyone again.

Honorable members, according to Article 94 of the Constitution of Nepal, constitutional bodies shall submit their annual reports of activities to the President, and the President shall cause that report to be presented to the Federal Parliament through the Prime Minister. Similarly, the Constitution also provides that the heads and officials of constitutional bodies shall be accountable and responsible to the Federal Parliament. In accordance with that provision, reports from constitutional bodies have been continuously presented to the National Assembly by the government. As per the provision in Rule 217 (c) of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, the Business Advisory Committee has decided to commence the practice of discussing reports in the House on its meeting dated Ashad 15, 2083. Therefore, it is informed that the discussion on the annual report of the National Inclusion Commission for the fiscal year 2081/082, which has already been presented to the House, will take place in the meeting scheduled for tomorrow, Ashad 26, 2083. The discussion and recommendations on the annual report of the constitutional bodies and the report on the implementation of the recommendations and suggestions mentioned in the report are expected to bring about significant improvement in implementation. Therefore, I also expect the active participation of the honorable members in tomorrow's discussion.

Honorable members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on Friday, Ashad 26, 2083, at 1:15 PM, and this meeting is hereby adjourned.

(Thereafter, the next meeting was adjourned to be held on Friday, Ashad 26, 2083, at 1:15 PM.)

Adjourned: 97:35.
